name.en-US: A Mirror that Flatters Not: On Conversion (1677)
name.pt-BR: Um espelho que não lisonjeia: Sobre a conversão (inglês, 1677)

description.en-US: The anonymous English of 1677 of Bernard's sermon to the clergy of Paris on conversion, cut by the translator into thirty-one chapters (the Maurist text has twenty-two, so this is its own book of the work), with his preface to all new converts and three more 'sermons' that are Bernard's first three Parables: the king's son, and the war between Babylon and Jerusalem.
description.pt-BR: A tradução inglesa anônima de 1677 do sermão de São Bernardo aos clérigos de Paris sobre a conversão, dividido pelo tradutor em trinta e um capítulos, com o prefácio do tradutor e três 'sermões' que são as três primeiras Parábolas de Bernardo.

sources.edition: A Mirror that Flatters Not: or, a Looking-glass for all New-Converts, that is, certain Sermons of St. Bernard translated into English (London, 1677), EEBO-TCP A27472.
sources.description: EEBO-TCP hand-keyed transcription, original spelling kept; long s printed as s. The 6 letters illegible in the source are restored, the word being in no doubt (h[…]gh, Bless[…]d). The printed list of faults (errata) is not applied. Raw TEI in sources/english-originals/.
sources.tierEvidence: Printed 1677; the TCP transcription is released to the public domain (CC0).

title.en-US: The Translator's Preface to All New-Converts
A Sermon Preached to the Clergy concerning Conversion
Chapter I. That no body can be converted to God, unless he be prevented by the Will of God, and by his Voice crying unto him within
Chapter II. That God's Voice offers it self to all, and presents it self to the Soul that's unwilling to hear it
Chapter III. That by the Voice of God the reasonable part of the Soul is made able to see, reprove, distinguish, and discern all its own miseries
Chapter IV. That he who loves Wickedness, hates both his own Soul and Body
Chapter V. Of the punishment as well of Soul as Body, and fruitless Repentance after death
Chapter VI. That the worm of Conscience ought here to be felt, and by little and little extinguished; and not to be cherished and nourished to immortality
Chapter VII. That to some it seems easy for man's will to obey the Divine Voice
Chapter VIII. How the will of man by Gluttony, Curiosity and Pride, and by all the senses of the Body rebels against the Divine Voice
Chapter IX. How the reasonable part of the Soul being now vexed and afflicted, is convinced of the vainly presumed facility, and confounded at the difficulty of this matter
Chapter X. A comfortable Respiration to the poor in Spirit
Chapter XI. That he cannot hope for the Kingdom of God, in whose flesh Sin does still reign
Chapter XII. The desires of Gluttony, and Lust, and other Vanities, what they will end in
Chapter XIII. Of the Slavery of Vices
Chapter XIV. Of the infidelity of Riches, and uncertainty of Death
Chapter XV. That the Works which we do in time, are as it were Seeds of Eternal Reward
Chapter XVI. That it is impossible for him that sins, so to hide himself, as not to be seen
Chapter XVII. What we may judg will become of those who live wickedly
Chapter XVIII. That the Spirit being enclined to good, the Flesh resists it
Chapter XIX. That we must Mourn, and after Mourning be Comforted
Chapter XX. That after Consolation we are to set our selves to Contemplate Heavenly things
Chapter XXI. That the Soul ought to take up its rest in this Contemplation
Chapter XXII. That being refreshed with the taste of Contemplation, he is made to understand Divine things
Chapter XXIII. That Sins that have been punished, and are not reiterated, cannot hurt us
Chapter XXIV. Of Mercy which is promised to the Merciful
Chapter XXV. That the Heart is to be cleansed, that God may be seen
Chapter XXVI. Of the Peaceable, Patient, and Peace-maker
Chapter XXVII. A Reprehension of the Ambitious, who having not their hearts cleansed, presume to pacify God towards others
Chapter XXVIII. That some usurp to themselves the degree of Peacemakers
Chapter XXIX. A Complaint against the Incontinent, for not Revering Holy Orders
Chapter XXX. An Exhortation to Repentance, that being first humbled, they may be afterwards exalted
Chapter XXXI. Of enduring Persecution, according to the last Beatitude
Three Sermons (the Parables)
Sermon I: Of the Spiritual Combat
Sermon II
Sermon III
